Commentary.Commentary: We are back after LUNCH! The Players and the Umpires have taken the field to start the England Second Innings with a lead of 46 runs and Ben Duckett and Zak Crawley are their opening batters. Ravichandran Ashwin to start the attack for India. Let's Play!
... DAY 3, SECOND SESSION ...

As England prepares to take their turn with the bat, holding a slender lead of 46 runs, the match's momentum hangs delicately in the balance. The stage is set for an intriguing battle in the upcoming sessions, as both teams vie for supremacy on a wicket that promises to be challenging for batting. The question looms, will England opt for an aggressive approach, reminiscent of Bazball? Or will they adopt a more measured strategy to set a challenging target for India? The answer to this question and more awaits us when the action resumes Post-Lunch on Day 3. Stay tuned as the drama unfolds in what promises to be a captivating continuation of this Test match. Join us at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT)

Dhruv Jurel emerged as the hero of the morning for India, exhibiting exemplary resilience and determination as he battled alongside the tail-enders to inch his team closer to England's total. His impressive innings of 90 runs provided a glimmer of hope for India after they faced a stern challenge from the English bowlers late yesterday. However, Jurel was eventually dismissed by Tom Hartley, bringing an end to India's innings. Credit must be given to England's bowlers, particularly Shoaib Bashir, who showcased his prowess by claiming his maiden five-wicket haul in Test cricket. Bashir's devastating spell dismantled the Indian middle order, providing England with crucial breakthroughs at crucial junctures.

LUNCH! As the players make their way off the field for the lunch break, we mark the conclusion of an eventful session that has seen the culmination of India's batting innings in this intriguing Test match. After a valiant effort by the Indian lower order, they have been bowled out for 307 runs, narrowing the gap to England's first-innings total to just 46 runs.

OUT! BOWLED'EM! England needed something special and Tom Hartley provides exactly that. Dhruv Jurel just misses out on his century but he has got the hosts back in this game. India have been bowled out for 307 and conceded a lead of 46 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to begin the 'Moving Day'! The two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the England players who spread out and take their respective field positions. Kuldeep Yadav and Dhruv Jurel are the overnight batters for India. Shoaib Bashir to bowl the first over of Day 3. Let's play...

Moreover, the fate of this Test match could be influenced by the unpredictable weather conditions. The forecast for Sunday suggests the possibility of showers in the afternoon, while Day 5 is expected to be cloudy with intermittent showers. Such conditions might further complicate the proceedings, adding another layer of uncertainty to the match. As the players take to the field, all eyes will be on India's lower order batters as they strive to chip away at England's lead and set up a competitive total. Stay tuned as the drama unfolds on what promises to be a captivating day of Test cricket.

After a stellar performance with the ball, cleaning up England for 353, India's batting order faced a stern test on Day 2. Unfortunately, big names like Rohit Sharma, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill, and Ravindra Jadeja have all returned to the pavilion, leaving the hopes of narrowing the deficit resting on the shoulders of Kuldeep Yadav and Dhruv Jurel. England's spinner, Shoaib Bashir, proved to be a thorn in India's side, claiming four crucial wickets for 84 runs. His scalps included the likes of Jaiswal, Gill, Rajat Patidar, and Jadeja, denting India's batting line-up significantly. With the pitch expected to assist spinners as the day progresses, India will need to navigate carefully against Bashir's threat. Adding to India's challenges, Tom Hartley also made significant contributions with the ball, dismissing Ravichandran Ashwin and Sarfaraz Khan, while the experienced James Anderson accounted for the prized wicket of Rohit Sharma.

Good morning and welcome to the start of Day 3 of this gripping Test match between India and England. As the sun rises over the field, we find ourselves at a crucial juncture in the game with India trailing England by 134 runs, standing at 219/7 in their first innings.
... DAY 3, FIRST SESSION ...

Right then, that concludes an eventful Day 2 of this Test match. England holds a slight advantage thanks to their bowling performance, but they'll aim to swiftly dismiss the hosts. India, meanwhile, will seek to accumulate as many runs as possible and narrow the gap. Day 3 is set to commence on 25th February, Sunday at 9:30 am IST (4 am GMT), but feel free to join us earlier for all the pre-match analysis. Cheers!

Joe Root, the centurion is up for a chat. He talks about the innings being a very special one as he was struggling with form and the team needed him to step up and get the job done and he is happy that he was able to do it. He talks about his reverse lap shot and says that this wicket is not very suitable for a shot like that and he was looking to play on the merit of the ball and get the runs. He talks about the young bowling attack of England and says that it looks like a good sign for the upcoming Ashes series.

In the third session, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sarfaraz Khan initially provided stability, but Stokes' astute captaincy applied pressure, making scoring difficult. Jaiswal fell victim to Shoaib Bashir, misjudging a delivery and dragging it onto his stumps. Shortly after, Sarfaraz departed to Tom Hartley's bowling, followed by Ravichandran Ashwin's dismissal. Despite the setbacks, Dhruv Jurel showcased defensive prowess and, alongside Kuldeep Yadav, ensured no further wickets fell before Stumps, adding crucial 42 runs for the hosts.

After Lunch, Shubman Gill settled in quickly and began scoring freely, finding the boundary regularly. Yashasvi Jaiswal, on the other hand, had to navigate through a testing spell from Ollie Robinson and survived a close call when an edge didn't carry to the keeper. Nonetheless, he showed resilience and brought up yet another half-century in this series. However, just as the partnership was blossoming, Shoaib Bashir trapped Gill lbw with a beautiful delivery, swinging momentum in England's favor. He then went on to dismiss Rajat Patidar and Ravindra Jadeja cheaply, further denting India's hopes before the end of the session. Despite the setbacks, Jaiswal remained steadfast, and Sarfaraz Khan joined him to initiate a rebuilding phase for the hosts.

The overnight partnership for England proved resilient, with Joe Root anchoring the innings with a gritty unbeaten century, frustrating the Indian bowlers. Meanwhile, Ollie Robinson played his shots freely and reached his maiden Test half-century. However, just before the hour mark, Robinson's attempt at something different cost him his wicket, followed by the quick dismissal of the last two batters. Despite this, England posted a commendable total of 353, a significant score on this wicket. When India came out to bat, the visitors applied pressure immediately, with veteran James Anderson removing the Indian skipper Rohit Sharma early on. However, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shubman Gill held firm for the rest of the session, ensuring no further damage to India's innings.

A captivating day of Test cricket draws to a close! Session Summary - 88 runs and 3 wickets in 35 overs! England will be pleased with their performance and have cemented their commanding position as we head into the crucial 'Moving Day'. Shoaib Bashir was the standout performer on Day 2, delivering a marathon spell and making crucial breakthroughs. He also achieved his best figures in first-class cricket with a four-fer and has the opportunity to improve upon them further. Although India finds themselves trailing by 134 runs, the resistance shown by Dhruv Jurel and Kuldeep Yadav offers hope for a resilient comeback when they resume their innings.

SESSION SUMMARY - 97 runs and 3 wickets in 28 overs! A hard-fought Test session draws to a close, with both teams giving their all after Lunch. The visitors managed to gain a slight edge in this period all thanks to a brilliant spell from Shoaib Bashir. Shubman Gill looked promising, finding the boundaries fluently, while Yashasvi Jaiswal faced some challenges against Ollie Robinson's impressive spell but persevered to reach his half-century. He did nick one behind but it just bounced before Ben Foakes and survived that scare. However, Gill fell victim to Bashir's off-spin, and Rajat Patidar also departed to Shoaib's bowling. Ravindra Jadeja, promoted up the order, showcased some aggressive strokes but was dismissed by Bashir just before Lunch. Jaiswal remained solid, aiming to build a partnership with Sarfaraz Khan to stabilize the hosts' innings. England will aim to capitalize on their breakthroughs and make further inroads in the last session. Join us at 2:30 am IST (9 am GMT) for the thrilling action in the final session.

... DAY 2, SECOND SESSION ...

As the players break for lunch, India trails by 319 runs in their first innings, with much riding on their performance in the upcoming sessions. Will they be able to mount a substantial total and narrow the deficit? The answers to these questions and more await as the action resumes post-lunch on Day 2. Stay tuned for what promises to be an intriguing afternoon session that starts at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT).

At the crease, Yashasvi Jaiswal has impressed with a brisk innings, remaining unbeaten on 27, showcasing his repertoire of elegant strokes. Alongside him, Shubman Gill is gearing up to provide the necessary support as India looks to build a solid foundation in response to England's imposing first innings total. Reflecting on the morning's play, England, starting the day at 302/7, rode on the masterful partnership between Joe Root and Ollie Robinson, propelling them to a respectable first innings total of 353. Root, in imperious form, departed unbeaten on a magnificent 122, steering his team to a substantial lead. However, India's bowlers staged a spirited fightback, claiming the remaining three wickets swiftly in the second hour of play, thereby limiting England's total and setting the stage for their batting effort.

SESSION SUMMARY- 24.5 Overs, 95 Runs, 4 Wickets. As the morning session draws to a close on Day 2 of this enthralling Test match, the players make their way back to the pavilion for a well-deserved lunch break. India, having commenced their innings after a disciplined bowling effort from England, find themselves at 34 for the loss of their skipper Rohit Sharma early in the proceedings.
